title: Contrast and tension in a speech
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Which two opposites does your talk hold in tension?
Jose said that last time he talked about alliteration, and that this time he would talk about symmetry in a speech, such as a tongue twister, where the sounds balance.
He said he would introduce concepts used in speeches, and asked whether that would be useful.
Jose said that dialectical tension and contrast are two concepts that are very good in politics: the yin and yang, black and white, two opposing views like a tug of war.
He asked what your stance should be when speaking to the masses in the middle of that tug of war, and a student answered that you identify your audience and the goal.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write two opposites in your message.
Write the sentence that holds both.
Write a line with matched sounds.
Write who is on each side of the rope.
Write where you stand and why.

check.q: What did Jose say last time's device was?
What is dialectical tension, as Jose described it?
choices: Two opposing views like a tug of war

check.q: What did a student say to identify?

recap: Use contrast and tension, with an audience and a goal.
